### Emission priority subtleties with ACKs pending and new results

Let's reread exact: "After every endpoint-valid input packet, and on flush/retry, the observable emission priority is: eligible pending upstream ACKs in ascending rank; then (on retry only) the selected receiver's previously sent but unacknowledged results in ascending q; then new results in ascending destination rank and q. Pending upstream ACK means E>U or a repeat was requested, with E>0. A failed result retransmission does not queue a continuation: a later retry starts again at the then-current downstream acknowledged prefix. New-result backlog and upstream ACK repeat requests remain pending as described. No result retransmission changes the new-output sent prefix. Empty/blocked/duplicate/stale/ignored-ACK opportunities still permit pending service. Wire-invalid or endpoint-invalid frames are simply dropped and do not trigger service. Retirement reflects all successful work from that opportunity, even if a later send fails. No automatic timer, ACK reception or fair drain is implicit. Unfinished inputs and permanent loss are valid finite traces."
